chunks: And from him (Al-Hassan ibn Mahbub) from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Umar ibn Yazeed who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has a guest from his brothers staying with him, and the day of Fitr arrives; should he pay the Fitrah on his behalf? He said: 'Yes, the Fitrah is obligatory upon every person who provides for a male or female, young or old, free or slave.'

And the newborn, if born on the night of Fitr, it is not obligatory to pay the Fitrah on his behalf; and likewise, whoever converts to Islam on the night of Fitr, it is not obligatory upon him to pay the Fitrah, according to what we mentioned. He narrated that.

key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Fitrah (Zakat al-Fitr), the alms-tax given at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.يَعُولُ: Provides for / supports (one who bears the financial responsibility)

ai.seo_question: Who is obligated to pay Zakat al-Fitr and are guests or newborns included?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that Zakat al-Fitr is a personal obligation on the head of the household for every dependent, including guests and slaves, reflecting the Shia view of familial responsibility. It further specifies that newborns and new converts on the night of Eid are exempt for that year, emphasizing the timing of the obligation relative to the sunset of the last day of Ramadan. This ruling underscores the social welfare aspect of Fitrah, ensuring all dependents are covered by the provider's charity.
